task_instance: Created a sample invoices.csv with 10 invoice records (invoice_no in column 1, header row) covering the range 1001-1013, seeded with 2 intentional duplicate invoice numbers (1002, 1010) and 3 gap ranges (1003; 1006-1007; 1011-1012). Ran the exact awk pipeline from SKILL.md against it, saved the output to sequence_findings.txt, and appended a short summary line for the auditor.
evidence: Commands run in work dir: `cut -d, -f1 invoices.csv | tail -n +2 | sort -n | awk 'NR>1 && $1==p {print "duplicate", $1} NR>1 && $1>p+1 {print "gap", p+1, "to", $1-1} {p=$1}'` piped through tee into sequence_findings.txt. Output produced: 'duplicate 1002', 'gap 1003 to 1003', 'gap 1006 to 1007', 'duplicate 1010', 'gap 1011 to 1012'. This exactly matches the seeded ground truth in invoices.csv (duplicates at 1002 and 1010; missing numbers 1003, 1006, 1007, 1011, 1012), confirming the awk check correctly detects gaps and duplicates. Verified by manual inspection of invoices.csv against the tool output. Files produced: invoices.csv, sequence_findings.txt (both in the work directory), the latter also containing the auditor summary line.
